statute_note: Principal source: the Government Printer PDF of Act No. 5 of 2017 as certified (text layer, 4 pages), parsed with parse_consolidated_pdf.py --edition as_enacted and then re-transcribed by hand because the parser split the single-column page at the wrong column and spliced every marginal note into the operative text. Other sources inspected: the paralegal.lk page text under statutes/HTML/ (agrees word for word; packaged as a verification source) and the older LLM extraction under statutes/parsed/ (comparison only). Consolidation cutoff: not applicable; this is the Act as enacted with no chain header and no markers. Review: all seven sections, both definitions, every marginal-note heading, the long title, the enacting formula, the certification and Gazette dates and the Legal Draftsman number were read word for word against pdftotext -layout output of the print; coverage check on the parser tree reported 461 source words, 2 unmatched (0.43%), both being the enumerators '2' and '3'; validate_finalized_trees.py reports 0 errors, 0 warnings. Amendment coverage: no amending instrument is known from the RUBRIK, the curriculum, the print or disk; nothing applied. Structural weaknesses: none known in the finalized tree; the canonical parser output under data/processed is not usable for this Act without the hand correction recorded in provenance.what_changed. Missing sources: none required. Unresolved questions: (1) the curriculum cites this Act as 'No. 7 of 2017' (data/legal-sources/conveyancing-source-checklist.md line 105, PRIMARY-STATUES.md line 106); the print, section 1 and the registry say No. 5 of 2017, and the registry note already records the correction; (2) the Act has no commencement section, so whether 2017-04-04 (certified) or 2017-04-07 (Gazette) is its commencement is for a lawyer; the tree carries the CSV value 2017-04-07 with a note; (3) the registry title capitalises 'Ground' where section 1 prints 'ground'. Lawyer verification: unverified. verification_status in the tree is structurally_verified, which speaks to structure and transcription against the print only, not legal effect.
